unit_label: Module A: International Banking - Facilities for Exporters and Importers

facts.statement: In the courseware's case study of an export finance account, the bank sanctions a pre-shipment limit and post-shipment sub-limits with stated margins. The packing credit against an order is the order value converted at the bank's bill buying rate, less an allowance for freight and insurance to reach the FOB value, less the sanctioned margin. The post-shipment advance on a usance bill is the bill value converted at the bill buying rate plus a forward premium for the period (usance plus transit), less the margin. The packing credit outstanding is adjusted from the proceeds of the discounted bill and the balance is credited to the exporter. The notional due date of a usance bill is the date of submission plus the usance period plus the normal transit period; interest on the advance is charged until the funds are credited to the bank's Nostro account, the effective date of realisation of a foreign currency bill.

payload.title: Case file: from order to packing credit
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case (all terms are assumptions stated here): a leather goods exporter has an order for USD 80,000 on CIF terms from a buyer in Germany. Its bank has sanctioned packing credit with a 20% margin on the FOB value and post-shipment finance on usance bills (documents against acceptance) with a 15% margin. The bank converts order values at its bill buying rate of ₹83.60 on the day the packing credit is released, and treats freight and insurance as 10% of the CIF value. What packing credit can the bank release against the order?

worked_steps.description: Convert the order value at the bill buying rate.
Remove freight and insurance (10% of the CIF value) to reach the FOB value.
Deduct the 20% margin on the FOB value.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: The bank can release packing credit of ₹48,15,360.00 against the order

self_check.prompt_text: Why is the margin taken on the FOB value and not the CIF value?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Freight and insurance are paid to others after shipment and are not part of what the exporter spends on producing the goods, so the bank finances the FOB value less its margin.

payload.title: Case file: discounting the bill, closing the packing credit
payload.core_explanation_md: Continuing the case: on 12 August 2026 the exporter submits documents for USD 78,000 against the order, drawn at 45 days after acceptance. The bank discounts the bill at its bill buying rate of ₹83.55 plus a forward premium of ₹0.12 for the usance period plus transit. The bank assumes a normal transit period of 25 days, and its policy is to close the packing credit of ₹48,15,360.00 from the bill proceeds and to credit the balance to the exporter. What is the purchase rate, the post-shipment advance, the balance credited, and the notional due date?

worked_steps.description: Purchase rate: bill buying rate plus the forward premium.
Advance after the 15% margin on a usance bill (85% advanced).
Close the packing credit from the advance and credit the rest.
Notional due date: submission date plus 45 days usance plus 25 days transit (70 days).

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Purchase rate ₹83.67; advance ₹55,47,321.00; ₹7,31,961.00 credited to the exporter after closing the packing credit; notional due date 21 October 2026

self_check.prompt_text: If the buyer's payment reaches the bank's Nostro account with value date 19 October 2026, up to which date is interest charged on the advance, and why?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Up to 19 October 2026: interest runs until the proceeds are credited to the bank's Nostro account, not until the notional due date.

payload.stem_md: An exporter has an order for USD 60,000 on CIF terms. The bank converts the order at its bill buying rate of ₹84.00, takes freight and insurance as 12% of the CIF value, and requires a 25% margin on the FOB value. What packing credit, in rupees, can the bank release?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the answer to 2 decimal places.

worked_solution_steps.description: FOB value after removing 12% freight and insurance

payload.stem_md: A usance bill (documents against acceptance) for USD 40,000 is discounted at a bill buying rate of ₹84.10 plus a forward premium of ₹0.15. The bank advances 85% of the rupee value. What is the post-shipment advance, in rupees?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the answer to 2 decimal places.

payload.stem_md: A usance bill is submitted on 12 August 2026 at 45 days after acceptance, and the bank applies a normal transit period of 25 days. What is the notional due date?

options.explanation_md: That is the due date without the transit period (45 days).

payload.correct_explanation_md: The notional due date is the submission date plus the usance period plus the normal transit period: 12 August 2026 plus 70 days is 21 October 2026.

payload.stem_md: Under the case study's method, up to which date is interest charged on an export bill that was discounted and later realised?

options.explanation_md: Interest is charged until the actual credit, not the notional date.

options.text_md: The date the proceeds are credited to the bank's Nostro account
options.explanation_md: This is the effective date of realisation of a foreign currency bill.

options.text_md: The date the buyer pays its own bank
options.explanation_md: The bank's own credit date governs.
Interest runs after discounting, until realisation.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Interest runs until the day the money reaches the bank's Nostro account, which is treated as the date of realisation.

payload.stem_md: In the case study method, why is the packing credit outstanding deducted from the post-shipment advance when a bill is discounted?

options.text_md: Because the exporter must repay the packing credit in cash first
options.explanation_md: Liquidation is from the bill proceeds.

options.text_md: Because margins are returned to the exporter
options.explanation_md: The margin is not returned in this step.

options.text_md: Because packing credit always carries a higher interest rate
options.explanation_md: The reason is liquidation, not rate.

options.text_md: Because the post-shipment advance liquidates the packing credit, which is closed from the bill proceeds

payload.correct_explanation_md: The post-shipment advance on the discounted bill liquidates the packing credit outstanding, and only the balance is credited to the exporter.

unresolved: The case study depends on a bank's own sanction terms and on the FEDAI normal transit period; every term is stated in the item as an assumption so that no regulatory rule is asserted. The courseware's own case figures (USD 50,000 and USD 48,000, 2021 dates) are not reused.
The courseware's answers (FOB deduction of 12%, a 25-day NTP, effective date of realisation) rest on FEDAI and bank practice that were not retrieved.
